Short title and commencement

PRESIDENT'S ORDER 8 OF 1970
PRESIDENT'S ORDER 8 OF 1970
HIGH COURTS (ESTABLISHMENT)
ORDER, 1970
1. Short title and commencement.‑( I) This Order may be
called the High Courts (Establishment) Order, 1970.
(2) It shall come into force at
once.

Definitions

PRESIDENT'S ORDER 8 OF 1970
PRESIDENT'S ORDER 8 OF 1970
HIGH COURTS (ESTABLISHMENT)
ORDER, 1970
2. Definitions.‑In this Order, unless there is anything
repugnant in the subject or context,‑
(1) "Circuit Court"
means any one or more Judges of a new High Court nominated by the Chief Justice
of that Court sitting or holding Court at a place within the territories for
which such High Court is established, other than its principal seat ;
(2) "new High Court"
means a High Court established by this Order;
(3) reference herein to an order
made by any High Court or a Judge shall be construed as including a reference
to any sentence, judgment or decree passed or made by that High Court or Judge;
and
(4) all other words and
expressions used but not defined in this Order shall have the same meanings
respectively as assigned to them in the said Order.

Establishment of High Courts for new provinces

PRESIDENT'S ORDER 8 OF 1970
PRESIDENT'S ORDER 8 OF 1970
HIGH COURTS (ESTABLISHMENT)
ORDER, 1970
3. Establishment of High Courts for new Provinces.‑(1) As
from the 1st day of July 1970, hereinafter referred to as the appointed day,
there shall be established the following new High Courts, namely:‑
(a) a High Court for the North‑West
Frontier Province to be called the Peshawar High Court with its principal seat
at Peshawar;
(b) a High Court for the Province of the Punjab and the Islamabad
Capital Territory to be called the Lahore High Court with its principal seat at
Lahore; and
(c) a High Court for the
Provinces of Baluchistan and Sind to be called the Sind and Baluchistan High
Court with its principal seat at Karachi.
(2) Each new High Court shall
be a Court of record and shall have such original, appellate and other
jurisdiction and such powers and authority in respect of the territories for
which it is established as 1 he High Court of West Pakistan, immediately before the
appointed day, had in respect of the territories in relation to which it
exercised appellate jurisdiction.
(3) Each new High Court and the
Judges and divisional Courts thereof shall sit at its principal seat but may
hold Circuit Courts at places within its territorial jurisdiction other than
its principal seat consisting of such of the Judges of the High Court as the
Chief Justice may from time to time nominate.

Appointment of Judges

PRESIDENT'S ORDER 8 OF 1970
PRESIDENT'S ORDER 8 OF 1970
HIGH COURTS (ESTABLISHMENT)
ORDER, 1970
4. Appointment of Judges.‑(1) Persons named in Schedule I shall,
as from‑ the appointed day, stand appointed as the Chief Justice or other
Judge of a new High Court as shown in that Schedule on the terms and conditions
not less favourable than those that were applicable to them immediately before
that day, and the service of such Chief Justice or Judge shall for the purposes
of pension and leave be deemed to be in continuation of previous service as
Chief Justice or Judge, as the case may be, of the High Court of West Pakistan:
Provided that an Additional
Judge shall, on such appointment, hold office until the expiry of the term of
his appointment unless he is appointed as permanent Judge in the meantime.
(2) A person appointed under
clause (1) shall before entering upon his office make oath in the form set out
in Schedule II as is appropriate to his office.
(3) Nothing in clause (1) shall
be construed as derogating from the power of the President to appoint one or
more Additional Judges to any of the new High Courts.

Sales of the High Courts

PRESIDENT'S ORDER 8 OF 1970
PRESIDENT'S ORDER 8 OF 1970
HIGH COURTS (ESTABLISHMENT)
ORDER, 1970
5. Seals of the High Courts.‑Each new high Court shall have a
seal bearing a device and impression of a crescent moon with horns pointing
upwards surmounted by a star, with an exergue or label surrounding the same
with an inscription indicating that it is the seal of that High Court, and the
said seal shall be delivered to and kept in the custody of the Chief Justice of
that High Court, and, in case of a vacancy in the office of the Chief Justice,
the seal shall be delivered to and kept in the custody of the Judge appointed
to act as the Chief Justice, and when so ever the office of the Chief Justice
or of the Judge to whom the custody of the seal is committed is vacant then the
High Court shall be and is hereby authorised and empowered to demand, seize and
take the said seal from any person or persons whomsoever by any means
whatsoever.

Form of writs, etc.

PRESIDENT'S ORDER 8 OF 1970
PRESIDENT'S ORDER 8 OF 1970
HIGH COURTS (ESTABLISHMENT)
ORDER, 1970
6. Form of writs
etc.‑The law in force immediately before the appointed day with respect
to the form of writs and other processes used, issued or awarded by the High
Court of West Pakistan shall, with necessary modifications, apply with respect
to the form of writs and other processes used, issued or awarded by any of the
new High Courts.

Powers of chief justice and other Judges

PRESIDENT'S ORDER 8 OF 1970
PRESIDENT'S ORDER 8 OF 1970
HIGH COURTS (ESTABLISHMENT)
ORDER, 1970
7. Powers of
Chief Justice anal other Judges.‑The
law in force imme diately before the appointed day relating to the powers of
the Chief Justice and of single Judges and divisional Courts of the High Court
of West Pakistan, and with respect to all matters ancillary to the exercise of
those powers, shall, with the necessary modifications, apply in relation to
each of the new High Courts.

Enforcement orders, etc. Of High Court of W.P.

PRESIDENT'S ORDER 8 OF 1970
PRESIDENT'S ORDER 8 OF 1970
HIGH COURTS (ESTABLISHMENT)
ORDER, 1970
8. Enforcement
Orders, etc., of High Court of
West Pakistan.‑(1) Subject to
the provisions of clause (2), any order made by the High Court of West Pakistan
before the appointed day shall as from that day and for all purposes be as
effective as if duly made by the new High Court of proper jurisdiction in the
matter.
(2) Where any such order as is mentioned in clause
(1) has whether before or after the appointed day, been confirmed, varied or
reversed on appeal, effect shall be given to the decision of the appellate
Court as if the order appealed from was an order of the new High Court having
proper jurisdiction in the matter.
(3) Any reference in this Article to the High Court
of West Pakistan shall be construed as including a reference to a Judge or
division thereof.

Power to transfer cases

PRESIDENT'S ORDER 8 OF 1970
PRESIDENT'S ORDER 8 OF 1970
HIGH COURTS (ESTABLISHMENT)
ORDER, 1970
9. Power to
transfer cases.‑On the
application of any of the parties, and after giving notice to the parties and
hearing such of them as desire to be heard, or of its own motion without such
notice, the Supreme Court may at any stage transfer for disposal any proceeding
pending before a new High Court to another new High Court.
